cx 0.8.0 puts your sessions in front of you when you are away from the terminal: on claude.ai and in the Claude app through Claude Code's own Remote Control, and on one page in any browser with `cx web`.

Claude still runs only on your servers, and the client still holds no credentials.

## Highlights

### Remote Control, named after the session

```sh
cx open -d web1:api@review --remote-control
cx rc on web1:api                    # every new session of this project
```

Claude Code's Remote Control puts a session on claude.ai/code and in the Claude app, with everything Claude Code does there: the conversation, approving its prompts, slash commands, interrupting it. cx starts a session with it and names it after its target, so `web1:api@review` is easy to find. Whether a session gets it is decided when it starts: by the flag, then the project's own setting (`cx rc`, kept on its server so every machine sees the same one), then the host's `#cx:remote_control=1`, then `CX_REMOTE_CONTROL`. `cx status` and `cx peek` show `rc` in MODE, and `cx peek --json` has the claude.ai link. Needs Claude Code signed in with a claude.ai account.

### `cx web`: every session in a browser

```sh
cx web                               # prints http://127.0.0.1:8377/#token=…
ssh -N -L 8377:127.0.0.1:8377 box    # from a phone or laptop, then open that link
```

One page, at phone width or on a desktop, in light or dark: every session on every server grouped by server and goal, blocked ones first, refreshing while you look. Open one to follow its conversation live, send it a message (through `cx nudge`, with the same refusals), open it in Claude, or start and stop it. A goals tab pauses, resumes and finishes goals.

Whoever can use that page can type into your sessions, and a session with no permission checks runs whatever it is told, so cx web is locked down by default: it listens on 127.0.0.1 only, every request needs a token (`~/.config/cx/web.token`, mode 0600, `cx web --rotate-token` to replace it), every change needs a CSRF token, nothing is sent cross-origin, and a message to a no-perms session needs its name typed back first. Reach it through an SSH tunnel or an authenticating reverse proxy; [docs/WEB.md](https://github.com/farajzadeh/cx/blob/v0.8.0/docs/WEB.md) has both, and the threat model.

The server is a small Go program with no dependencies. `install.sh` downloads this release's build for your platform and checks it against `SHA256SUMS`; without one, `cx web` builds it once with Go 1.21+.

### Watching a session's own screen

`cx open --view web1:api@review` attaches to a running session read-only, without resizing its window under whoever is working in it. `cx web --terminal` shows the same screen in the browser through [ttyd](https://github.com/tsl0922/ttyd), behind cx web's sign-in.

### `cx tail`

A session's conversation as text or `--json`, main thread only. Given the cursor from its last answer it reads only what was written since, which is what `cx web` streams.

## Upgrading

1. Update the client. From a clone:

   ```sh
   git pull && ./install.sh
   ```

   or re-run the one-liner:

   ```sh
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farajzadeh/cx/main/install.sh | bash
   ```

   `cx --version` should print `cx 0.8.0`.

2. Update the agent on every server:

   ```sh
   cx provision --all
   ```

   Remote Control, `cx web`'s live view, `cx tail` and `cx open --view` need agent 0.8.0, and say so against an older one.

## Behaviour changes

- **`cx peek` has a MODE column** between STATE and WHO: the permission mode a session was started with (`no-perms` for none) and `rc` for Remote Control. A script that splits the table on whitespace sees one more column; `--json` is the stable form.
- **`cx doctor` reports a server as signed in only when it is.** It used to count any `~/.claude.json`, which Claude Code writes the first time it runs, so a server nobody had signed in to looked signed in and `cx open` skipped its warning.

Full details, including everything fixed: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/farajzadeh/cx/blob/v0.8.0/CHANGELOG.md).
